question: Which of the following novels is based on Malgudi, a fictional town in south India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Guide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The Guide**, written by R.K. Narayan, is one of the most celebrated novels in Indian English literature.
 
• The novel is set in the fictional town of **Malgudi**, which serves as the backdrop for many of R.K. Narayan's works.
 
• Malgudi is a fictional South Indian town created by R.K. Narayan to depict everyday life in a small Indian town.
 
• **The Guide** won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1960, making R.K. Narayan one of the first Indian authors to receive the honor.
 
• The book was adapted into a critically acclaimed Bollywood movie, **Guide**, in 1965, starring Dev Anand and Waheeda Rehman.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **R.K. Narayan:**

 
 
• R.K. Narayan (1906-2001) is one of the pioneers of Indian English literature.
 
• He is known for his simple yet profound storytelling, often rooted in Indian culture and traditions.
 
• His other notable works include **Swami and Friends**, **The Bachelor of Arts**, and **The English Teacher**.
 
 
 
• **Malgudi:**
 
 
• Malgudi is a fictional town created by R.K. Narayan to reflect the essence of a typical South Indian town.
 
• The town combines Indian traditions with modernity, serving as a microcosm of Indian society.
 
• It first appeared in his novel **Swami and Friends** (1935).
 
 
 
• **The Guide - Themes:**
 
 
• The novel explores themes like personal transformation, love, greed, and spirituality.
 
• The protagonist, Raju, evolves from being a tourist guide to a spiritual leader in the story.
 
 
 
• **Indian English Literature:**
 
 
• Indian English literature refers to works written by Indian authors in the English language.
 
• Prominent authors include R.K. Narayan, Mulk Raj Anand, Raja Rao, and more recently, Arundhati Roy and Salman Rushdie.
 
• It often highlights Indian traditions, societal changes, and historical events.
